stem: The number of speakers in 2020 was $k$ times the number of speakers in 2000. What is the value of $k$?
stimulus: A linguist tracking a regional dialect found that its number of fluent speakers fell by 15% from 2000 to 2010. From 2010 to 2020, the number of fluent speakers rose by 20%.
explanation: Turn each percent change into a multiplier. A 15% decrease means multiplying by $1 - 0.15 = 0.85$. A 20% increase means multiplying by $1 + 0.20 = 1.2$. When changes happen one after another, you multiply them: $k = (0.85)(1.2) = 1.02$. Don't add the percents. The 20% increase is taken of the smaller 2010 count, not the 2000 count, so the net change is +2%, not +5%.

common_errors.why: Added the percents (−15% + 20% = +5%) instead of multiplying the multipliers.
Found the net change as a bare rate (2%) and entered 0.02 instead of the multiplier 1 + 0.02.
Used 0.8 for the 20% increase, as if it were a decrease: (0.85)(0.8) = 0.68.
Used 1.15 for the 15% decrease, as if it were an increase: (1.15)(1.2) = 1.38.
Used only the 2010–2020 change and ignored the first decade.

stem: The percent coral cover at Reef A is $k$ times the percent coral cover at Reef C. What is the value of $k$?
stimulus: Marine biologists measured the percent of seafloor covered by living coral at three reefs. The coral cover at Reef A is 40% greater than the coral cover at Reef B. The coral cover at Reef B is 25% less than the coral cover at Reef C.
explanation: Write each comparison as a multiplier, using the quantity after "than" as the base. "40% greater than B" gives $A = 1.4B$. "25% less than C" gives $B = 0.75C$. Substitute: $A = 1.4(0.75C) = 1.05C$, so $k = 1.05$. Don't add or subtract the percents, and keep C as the base of the second comparison.

common_errors.why: Combined the percents by adding (40% − 25% = 15%) instead of multiplying 1.4 and 0.75.
Entered the bare rate of the 5% difference instead of the multiplier 1.05.
Used 1.25 for "25% less than", treating it as an increase: (1.4)(1.25) = 1.75.
Reversed the base of the second comparison, reading it as "C is 25% more than B", so B = C/1.25 = 0.8C and A = (1.4)(0.8)C = 1.12C.
Used only the A-to-B comparison and never connected B to C.

stem: The total mass of sugar in one serving of the new cereal is $k$ times the total mass of sugar in one serving of the original cereal. What is the value of $k$?
stimulus: A food company reformulated a breakfast cereal. In the new recipe, the mass of sugar per gram of cereal is 25% less than in the original recipe. The company also increased the serving size, so one serving of the new cereal has 10% more mass than one serving of the original cereal.
explanation: Sugar per serving = (sugar per gram) × (grams per serving), so each factor's multiplier carries through to the product. Sugar per gram is multiplied by $1 - 0.25 = 0.75$. Grams per serving is multiplied by $1 + 0.10 = 1.1$. So sugar per serving is multiplied by $k = (0.75)(1.1) = 0.825$.

common_errors.why: Added the percent changes (−25% + 10% = −15%) and used 1 − 0.15 instead of multiplying the multipliers.
Entered the size of the decrease (17.5%) as a rate instead of the multiplier 1 − 0.175.
Used 1.25 for the 25% decrease, as if it were an increase: (1.25)(1.1) = 1.375.
Applied only the change in sugar concentration and ignored the larger serving size.

stem: The cartographer wants to multiply each displayed distance by a number $k$ so that every distance returns to its length on the original display. What is the value of $k$?
stimulus: A cartographer changes the scale of a digital map so that every distance shown on the screen is 40% shorter than it was on the original display.
explanation: First write the change as a multiplier. A 40% decrease multiplies each original distance $d$ by $1 - 0.40 = 0.6$, so the new distance is $0.6d$. To get back to $d$, solve $k(0.6d) = d$. That gives $k = \frac{1}{0.6} = \frac{5}{3}$. Undoing a 40% decrease is not a 40% increase. The 40% was taken of the original length, but the increase has to be taken of the smaller, shortened length.

common_errors.why: Assumed a 40% increase undoes a 40% decrease. It doesn't: 0.6 × 1.4 = 0.84, not 1.
Gave the multiplier for the scale change itself instead of the multiplier that reverses it.
Entered the bare rate of the decrease instead of any multiplier.
Inverted the wrong quantity, computing 0.4/0.6 instead of 1/0.6.
